methods.label: Four quarters make one circle
methods.explanation:
The four white quarter circles on one tile together have the area of one full circle of radius \(\frac12\) foot. Their interiors do not overlap: the radius is half the tile's side length, so adjacent white pieces meet only at side midpoints. Their total white area is therefore
\[
\pi\left(\frac12\right)^2=\frac{\pi}{4}
\]
square foot. Each tile has area \(1\) square foot, leaving shaded area \(1-\frac{\pi}{4}\).

There are \(8\cdot10=80\) tiles, so the floor's shaded area is
\[
80\left(1-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=80-20\pi
\]
square feet, choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
methods.levelReason: The solution uses square and circle areas, subtraction of areas, and multiplication across identical tiles.
